title: Victorian stream-side water tables fell to the drainage line after 1997, but runoff stayed low at the pre-1997 connection state (141 bores, 30 catchments)
abstract: Question: after 1997, south-east Australian runoff stayed 20-25% below its 1951-1996 rainfall-runoff relation. Earlier campaign studies found that Victorian water tables fell about 1 m and proposed that streams became disconnected from groundwater. We tested this threshold mechanism directly. Approach: for 1,016 Victorian WMIS bores near 105 CAMELS-AUS v2.03 catchments, we calculated the height above nearest drainage from the Geoscience Australia 1-second hydrologically enforced DEM (DEM-H) and the head above the drainage line (HAND minus depth to water). The primary set was 141 shallow bores within 500 m of a 5 km2 channel inside 30 catchments. The runoff deficit came from the annual model Q = a + bP + cP(t-1) + dT fitted on 1951-1996 (AGCD rain; SILO check). The plan was written before any comparison. Results: the median stream-side head fell from +0.47 m to -0.39 m relative to the drainage line; the share above it fell from 59% to 45%; 14% of bores (CI 9-21%) crossed below and none crossed back, but all crossings were within the 2.4 m DEM error. The planned cross-catchment link was not supported (Spearman rho 0.21, CI -0.09 to 0.53). Catchments in which no stream-side bore crossed still lost 20% of runoff (CI -48 to -10%). The head fall above the drainage line did not predict the deficit better than the total fall. Post hoc: in a fixed bore panel the connected share fell as much from 1985-1989 to 1990-1996 (0.77 to 0.67) without runoff loss as it did after 1997; in 2011 it returned to the 1990-1996 level while runoff was 45% low; in 1997-2021 years with a connected share at or above the pre-1997 level, runoff was still 14% low (CI -32 to -0%), about 70% of the deficit in other years. Zero-flow days rose equally in all classes. An aridity-adjusted class difference (-20 points) did not survive a 2 m change of the threshold. Conclusion: stream-side water tables moved to the drainage line, but stream-groundwater disconnection is not the general cause of the persistent runoff loss; a smaller local share is possible. Limitations: DEM vertical error near the size of the head changes; bores are not at the stream; 30 catchments in 12 one-degree cells; Victoria only; several key tests are post hoc.

Runoff stayed low at matched bore levels; we find the same at matched stream-side connection state.

Nested gauges showed small channel losses; we also find no disconnection signal in the deficit.
